units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
After a while, looks up and remains resting upon his elbow.

If it had only been something inherited--something one wasn't responsible for! But this! To have thrown away so shamefully, thoughtlessly, recklessly, one's own happiness, one's own health, everything in the world--one's future, one's very life--!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: No, no, my dear, darling boy; this is impossible!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Bends over him.
Things are not so desperate as you think.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Oh, you don't know--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Springs up.
And then, mother, to cause you all this sorrow! Many a time I have almost wished and hoped that at bottom you didn't care so very much about me.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: I, Oswald? My only boy! You are all I have in the world! The only thing I care about!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Seizes both her hands and kisses them.

Yes, yes, I see it. When I'm at home, I see it, of course; and that's almost the hardest part for me.--But now you know the whole story and now we won't talk any more about it to-day. I daren't think of it for long together.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Goes up the room.
Get me something to drink, mother.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: To drink? What do you want to drink now?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Oh, anything you like. You have some cold punch in the house.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, but my dear Oswald--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Don't refuse me, mother. Do be kind, now! I must have something to wash down all these gnawing thoughts.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Goes into the conservatory.
And then--it's so dark here!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: MRS. ALVING pulls a bell-rope on the right.
And this ceaseless rain! It may go on week after week, for months together. Never to get a glimpse of the sun! I can't recollect ever having seen the sun shine all the times I've been at home.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Oswald--you are thinking of going away from me.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: H'm--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Drawing a heavy breath.
--I'm not thinking of anything. I cannot think of anything!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: In a low voice.
I let thinking alone.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: From the dining-room.
Did you ring, ma'am?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Yes; let us have the lamp in.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, ma'am. It's ready lighted.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Goes out.
Goes across to OSWALD.
Oswald, be frank with me.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Well, so I am, mother.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Goes to the table.
I think I have told you enough.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: REGINA brings the lamp and sets it upon the table.
Regina, you may bring us a small bottle of champagne.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Very well, ma'am.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Goes out.
Puts his arm round MRS. ALVING's neck.
That's just what I wanted. I knew mother wouldn't let her boy go thirsty.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: My own, poor, darling Oswald; how could I deny you anything now?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Eagerly.
